candidate_statement: "Changes are pushed directly to `main`."
"Every push must leave CI green; a red `main` is fixed before any other work."
"Tools are written in TypeScript and share one core library."
"Python and Java are used only for CI oracles and the SysML v2 parser gate; users never run them."
"A rule with status Unreviewed is visible but not binding."
"No build work may depend on an Unreviewed rule until the owner sets it to Active."
"Rules live in `governance/RULESET.md` only."
"Decisions that create, change or retire a rule are recorded in `governance/DECISIONS.md` and name the rule they change."
"MDSE_v2 is the single home for MDSE rules, schemas and tools."
"Test_Vault_ and MDSE_Workbench are read-only archives; nothing in them overrides this repository."
"Claude may push directly to main on Test_Vault_."
"Topics are decided one at a time."
"AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md is the one set of AI instructions."
"AGENTS.md at the root is a pointer to it."
"One clean Translator Definition file states what the stage 1 translator must do and is updated whenever a change is made."
"The import reads the .qeax directly"
"CSV files only defined the rules."
"Obsidian-native-first: prefer representations native to core Obsidian, then conventional Markdown/YAML, and use custom syntax only when needed."
"Tool ownership: Workbench owns UI behavior, disposable index, ModelRef navigation, schema-valid edit transactions and Review disposition (not semantics, importer mapping or release packaging)."
"Bootstrap owns safe activation repair, release verification and author registration."
"Importer owns source translation, naming/identity allocation and import evidence (not editing or plugin management)."
"Base builder owns the runtime payload, governed plugin config and pins/hashes."
"Cross-vault is deferred (archived resolver is reference only). A tool may not silently broaden or redefine model semantics; archived material never overrides a current source."
"One vault in phase 1."
"No cross-vault links."
"Final vault holds engineering notes plus a few definitions and diagrams."
"Methodology and translation material stays out of it."
"Test_Vault_ is a workspace, not the built vault."
"Final folder structure follows the EA package structure. 99_System is kept and edited topic by topic."
"Legacy empty model folders were removed."
"Safety: QEAX, BOM originals, private ledgers, EA identifiers and generated real model content stay out of public Test_Vault_."
"Never claim native certification from source normalization or parser-only syntax acceptance."
"Public repos hold synthetic content only."
"No real product names, BOMs, drawings, customers, revision histories or source exports."
"Real models are imported only in a private/local environment. A scan is a backstop, not a guarantee."
"Test_Vault_ stays the method and tool authority."
"Templates serve hand-authored and translated notes and are the single definition of a class."
"Every note gets uid and id filled automatically."
"Outside material keeps its own identification."
"Duplicate ids are handled by a periodic AI sweep."
"Author code is 13 characters: last name then first name, lowercase letters only, truncated to 13, padded right with hyphens."
"Authors are mapped from EA Author values to codes in authors.yaml."
"Login and display names of one person are one author."
"uid timestamp (yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS) is local time, not UTC."
"Translated notes carry EA creation time exactly as stored."
"Every id uses a five-digit number (for example REQ-00042)."
"An id is never reused."
"A note is retired, not deleted: status Retired, id stays reserved. A validator flags gaps in numbering."
"Templates fill uid and id through two Templater snippets. id is the prefix plus highest existing number plus one, counting retired notes and formerIds."
"AI author code is tool name, then ai, then hyphens to 13 characters."
"Tool names longer than 11 letters are cut to 11."
"People are one note each in 99_System/04_People, from a Person template (code, name, timezone, previousCodes, eaNames)."
"The id snippet and AI instructions count ids listed under ## Former ids when finding the highest number."
"One global 30-character identity-token namespace spans notes and Local Model records; a token is never reused."
"The kind prefix (part-, ep-, conn-, flow-) is not a separate namespace. A promoted local entity keeps its token."
"Translated notes carry the original EA creation time and author in uid."
"Each person enters their name once; the author code is generated by one written rule at install (Bootstrap) and on first template use."
"EA elements with no usable author get the code sparxeaauthor."
"Translated notes get ids numbered per class prefix in EA creation order, ties by EA GUID, no gaps."
"Numbers permanent after final migration."
"Requirements that share an external designator take internal STD- or STK- ids; the designator is kept as a `Designator` line in the `## Source: EA` section."
"Standard requirements take STD-#####; stakeholder requirements take STK-#####; other Requirement subtypes keep REQ-#####."
"Numbered in EA creation order, ties by EA GUID."
"No designator parsing."
"Withdraws the external-id form of W-17 for standards."
"Source lineage EA8647; source identity is EA8647 + EA GUID, kept in importer provenance only."
"First allocation uses EA Created as written (no time zone conversion, missing ms = 000), the normalized EA author code, or skellyspencer if unusable."
"Every model note has an immutable 30-character `uid` in the form `yyyyMMddHHmmssSSS` plus a 13-character author code."
"The `uid` never changes after creation."
"`id` is `PREFIX-NNNNN`, with the prefix from the class in `element-types.yaml`."
"The primary reusable engineering type is `Object`."
"`Thing` is deprecated."
"`type` is the semantic class."
"`subtype` is an approved classification within that type."
"`kind` is deprecated."
"`subtypeOf` is used only for a reusable invariant semantic distinction."
"Ordinary data or configuration variation is not a `subtypeOf`."
"Notes in `99_System` carry no `type` or `subtype`."
"Search for an existing authoritative definition before creating a new one."
"Prefer reuse, then instance, then specialization, then decomposition, then a new concept."
"The old eaGUID appears only at the bottom of the note body, for traceability."
"Not a frontmatter property."
"Relationship fields follow tags in the order of relationships.yaml and may hold lists."
"Legacy folder values are removed from element-types.yaml, except Diagram (72_Diagrams)."
"Notes in 99_System carry no type or subtype but keep id, uid and status."
"Hand-made class templates end with ## Notes, ## Aliases and ## Former ids, in that order (modelCheck excepted)."
"Every property has its own definition note: what it is, how determined, what it impacts."
"Property definition notes live in Definitions/Properties, one per property, named exactly as the property. A Base lists them."
"A translated note ends includes a Source: EA section."
"EA GUID line is first; other kept EA values go below it, one per line."
"Only real values are written."
"Template fields are always present in a note."
"A source field that has no data and is not a template field is not written to the YAML."
"`eaGUID` appears only at the bottom of notes translated from EA."
"It is not in frontmatter."
"MDSE entities are Object (not Thing)."
"Notes use type and subtype (not kind)."
"EA's own metaclass is written EA Object."
"There is no provisional relationship field. A link whose relationship cannot be resolved is recorded as a `flagLink`."
"supersedes/supersededBy is kept for elements replaced by another note."
"Nothing in the import writes it."
"Relationship endpoint rules (allowed source and target classes) live on each relationship in relationships.yaml."
"Inverse relationship fields are written by the translator and Workbench, not Nodian."
"The forward field wins when they disagree."
"`aliasOf` says a note is the same part as another and is waiting to be merged: a one-way link written on the note that will go away, pointing at the note that stays, Object to Object only."
"It is removed by the merge or by clearing it; no inverse is written."
"Full-import usability amendments: folder structure is navigation, no count-based splits, about 5 to 6 folder levels, a one-child folder collapses only when it has no independent value."
"Anything SysML v2 can define (structure, usages, relationships SysML defines) is written only in the note's `## SysML v2` block."
"Everything else (MDSE classification, identity, provenance, descriptive and review links SysML does not define) is written in YAML frontmatter."
"Nothing is written in both places."

"New development goes in the v2 workspace (numbered 20+ folders). V1 is frozen reference evidence. A v2 change never modifies 10_*, 11_* or other v1 areas without explicit cross-version approval; shared changes must be compatible with both pipelines."
"Phased release: first usable release is validated EA import plus read-only Workbench; graphical editing and the BOM importer are later phases but their interfaces are kept."

"Hybrid managed configuration: core plugin and schema compatibility is centrally governed, approved personal preferences survive updates, with versioned ownership, migration, dry-run diff and rollback before distribution."
"Cross-vault: design IDs, links and resolver now, ship after single-vault validation."

"Non-negotiable: approved mappings are not reopened because implementation is incomplete; native OMG SysML v2 only, with non-native MDSE evidence and review flags distinct; V2 builds independently of archived V1; each source element and connector gets an auditable disposition with zero hidden drops; syntax parsing, semantic validation, end-user UI and package/release acceptance are different gates."
"The parser gate is run in CI and on a maintainer's machine."
"The ZIP carries a parser-check report."
"Workbench marks the report stale after any SysML change."
"Changes to the `## SysML v2` section by import require approval"
"Rules and documentation refer to \"the latest version\" of a schema or tool."
"Exact pinned versions appear only in the release manifest."
"The schemas in force are the latest versions in `governance/schemas/`."
"Rules never name a schema version; pinned versions live only in the release manifest"
"authors.yaml: defaultTimezone America/Los_Angeles"

"AI authors claudeai-----, chatgptai----, rovoai-------, geminiai-----; a user-directed note uses the user's code even if an AI wrote it; the generic unmapped fallback sparxeaauthor is overridden by skellyspencer for the EA8647 import."
"A flag is an Obsidian callout whose type names the issue."
"Types: `flagImport`, `flagConflict`, `flagLink`, `flagNote`."
"New types are added to this section before use."
"The importer and AI processes add flags."
"Only an engineer removes a flag, after the issue is resolved."
"The SysML v2 language is documented one note per construct (element and relationship) in `governance/language/`, built from `catalog.json`."

"Each note gives the description, the elements it can come from and go to, what separates it from the most similar construct, an example, and how often engineers use it (Everyday, Common, Occasional, Rare)."
"The notes ship in every vault under `99_System/04_Language`."
"Every example in the language catalog is recognized by the Workbench scanner as that construct, with no warnings. A statement the scanner cannot classify is reported, never dropped."
"Import is mechanical."
"The importer applies the Ruleset and does not interpret."
"Every change to an existing file is listed in one dated changelog per import run."
"Each entry links the changed file, describes the change, and flags any conflict."
"Importing the same input again produces no changes and no changelog entries."
"Import is additive."
"An import never deletes existing content."
"An empty YAML property may be filled by an import."
"Content that does not match existing body content is added to the body."
"A change to any existing value requires approval, including EA-owned fields."
"Approval is given before the run (pre-approval, by field selection in the Start step) or after the run (review approval)."
"Pre-approval applies to all notes in the run."
"A conflict is content that contradicts existing YAML, v2, or body content and is not approved for change."
"It is not applied."
"It is listed in the body with a `flagConflict` callout for engineer review."
"An engineer resolves a conflict by approving a change or by selecting the correct data by hand."
"A source record that disappears is reported with a `flagImport` callout."
"It is not deleted."
"This applies to EA-owned relationships."
"A content change made by an engineer is not changed by an import unless approved."
"Add-onto-existing matches a note by `uid`, not by path."
"Tagged values follow `governance/schemas/ea-tag-dispositions.json` (the V1 list, 121 tags, decisions W-29 to W-106)."

"Only `body` tags are written to `## Source: EA`. A value that is empty, `unassigned` or `<memo>` is never written, whatever its tag. A tag not in the list is kept in the body and reported as an import warning until it is given a disposition."
"`## Source: EA` carries one EA GUID, the note's own, as the re-import identity."
"Usage, relationship, flow, trigger and connector lines carry no GUID; they name the other note. A flag callout keeps the connector GUID because it is the handle to the ledger row."

"A Part, Port or Action usage with no name of its own takes the name of its typed element, made unique within its owner (`pCE25ECU`, then `pCE25ECU_2`). A usage with neither a name nor a resolvable type keeps a generated name and is flagged."
"Structure, links, quantities and multiplicity are defined by the SysML v2 block and are not repeated in `## Source: EA`."
"Relationships SysML v2 has no form for, and identifying properties, stay in the YAML (`describes`, `eaType`, `uid`, `id`)."

"`## Source: EA` holds only what is stored nowhere else: the note's EA GUID, the original name when the file name differs, alias, the kept tags, trigger and guard text, unresolved connectors and attachments."
"EA author, created date, type, stereotype and package are not written: the uid carries date and author, `eaType` carries type and stereotype, the folder carries the package."
"A requirement's wording is the `doc /* … */` of its `requirement def` (EA Note plus `text` tags), and is not repeated in the note body."
"Anywhere the Workbench shows a requirement it shows name, subtype and text."
"Transition trigger, guard and effect follow SysML v2: `transition first a accept t if g do e then b;` and `succession first a if g then b;`, with the wording in `doc` of helper usages."
"EA PDATA1/2/3 are trigger/guard/effect."

"The importer page asks for the person's full name before anything can be built, derives the 13-character author code (MOD-002), remembers it in the browser, and uses it as the vault's `author`, as the author of every note created in the run, and for the person note in `99_System/04_People` of a new vault."
"It cannot be dismissed without a name."

"The page shows a stage progress bar with a labelled list of stages (fingerprint, translate EA, map BOM, assemble, write), and ends with the Obsidian steps: open the vault, click \"Trust author and enable plugins\", let Bootstrap verify and enable, confirm with the Bootstrap command."
"It says plainly that the trust click cannot be automated."
"An EA Port becomes a port usage written `port name : [~]PortDef[mult]`."
"The type is the Port's PDATA1 (an EA interface Class, which is a port definition, IMP-104); the Classifier field is not the type."
"The multiplicity is the Multiplicity field, read as for parts"

"`~` is written when the object has an `isConjugated` tag with a true value (`true`, `yes`, `1` or EA's `-1`). A Port whose PDATA1 is not a port definition (a connector, a signal) is written without a type, the target is kept as a `- Port <name> is typed by [[…]]` line in Source, and the usage is flagged (`UNRESOLVED_PORT_TYPE:TARGET_IS_…`)."

"A file or folder name is made safe for the browser's folder writer and for Windows: no control, bidi, line-separator or special characters, no lone surrogates, no trailing dot or space, and a device name (Con, Aux, Nul, Prn, Com0-9, Lpt0-9) is reserved with any extension, so `Con.pdf` becomes `Con_.pdf`."
"The page checks every path before writing anything and lists any that would fail; a write error names its path."

"No folder or file name is cut to fit a path length; the 400-character path limit is handled after the import, not by the importer. A name is changed only for the safety rules of IMP-102 (the 150-character part limit, which is marked)."

"The folder write retries a file up to six times with a growing delay on InvalidStateError, NoModificationAllowedError or NotReadableError (antivirus, cloud sync or the indexer touching a new file), and a write error names the browser error, its message and the path."

"An EA Class with an interface stereotype (Electrical & Material, Data, Mechanical, Generic Physical, Environmental) is written as a `port def`, because EA types ports by it (3,328 of 3,425 PDATA1 port types point at one)."
"`interface def` is left for connection kinds written in the Workbench. (V1 W-113, W-120; D-0037)"

"PDATA1, PDATA2 and PDATA3 of an object hold the GUID (`{…}`) of another element; a plain Object_ID is also accepted. A Part's block, a Port's type and a FlowProperty's Signal come from PDATA1; a Port's instance link from PDATA3. (V1 W-44, W-113; D-0037)"
"A Port under a Part is the Part's block's own port and is not written as a usage of the Part."

"It merges, with one hop and never up the redefinition chain: (1) PDATA3 names a Port owned by the Part's block; (2) else the block has exactly one port with the same non-blank name; (3) else it is added to the block as a port of its own, flagged for review, and same-named ones on one block combine. A Part with no block defers the Port (`USAGE_WITHOUT_NOTE_OWNER`). A merged Port types an untyped block port from its PDATA1. (V1 W-114, W-130; D-0037)"

"A Part inside an action definition that points (PDATA1) at an action definition is an `action name : Target;` there; inside a state definition pointing at a state definition it is a `state name : Target;`. (V1 W-137, REG-113; D-0037)"
"A connector whose end is a Part acts on the block that Part points at (PDATA1), not on the usage: a requirement satisfied or allocated by a Part is satisfied by its block."
"A connector between Ports on Parts of one assembly is written in that assembly as `connect partA.port to partB.port`; a Port on a Part and a boundary Port of the assembly connect the same way."
"Other port connections follow IMP-049."

"An EA Object points at the Class it is a kind of through Classifier; its part def specializes that Class's part def (`:>`), never typed by it. (V1 W-135, approved exception on Object classifiers; D-0037)"

"A usage name is the EA name made into a SysML identifier with a lower first letter, except that a name that starts with two capitals (an acronym) keeps its case: `USB-MCU` is `USBMCU`, `CAN TXRX` is `CANTXRX`, `LED Port` is `LEDPort`, not `uSBMCU`, `cANTXRX`, `lEDPort`."

"An Aggregation or Composition makes the child a usage in the whole, of the kind its two definitions are: part/part is `part`, action/action `action`, state/state `state`, item/item `item`, requirement/requirement `requirement`, part/port def `port`, use case/use case `use case`."
"The whole is the end marked composite or shared."
"Every connector is its own usage, even with the same two ends; it takes the child end's role name, else the child's name with `_2` suffixes, and the child end's multiplicity (none is invented)."

"An EA Part or nested element of that type is matched to one connector and not repeated. A connector whose whole and part sit in one cycle of ownership is left out as OWNERSHIP_CYCLE. A part that is the child of an interface is AGGREGATION_PART_IN_INTERFACE (review). (Test_Vault_ approved aggregation docs 2026-10-17; D-0038)"

"An element nested (ParentID) under one of its own kind is a usage of it in the owner: activity in activity or in a state or verification case is `action x : X;`, state in state `state x : X;`, requirement in requirement `requirement x : X;`."
"Folders, notes and files do not change."
"Nesting of other kinds stays organizational. (Test_Vault_ nested states/activities, other-nesting and nested-requirement approvals; D-0038)"

"A relationship end that is an MDSE note (Issue, Change, Info, Artifact, Decision) has no SysML form and becomes a YAML link on the source note: `describes` when the note is Info, Artifact or Document, `dependsOn` for Dependency and Usage, `hasChild` for Aggregation, and otherwise the provisional `tracesTo` with PROVISIONAL_LINK."
"Source: EA does not repeat the link."
"ControlFlow and StateFlow between usages, or between definitions nested in one owner, are a `succession` or `transition` in that owner."
"Between notes that share no owner they are the `precedes` link on the step before, with trigger, guard and effect as a Source line (V1 W-174, W-175)."

"Realisation finds the part by element type, not arrow direction: part and action is `perform`; requirement and part is `allocate REQ to Part`, never satisfy; part and part is `allocate`. (Test_Vault_ Object/Requirement realization decision; D-0038)"
"An Association between a Use Case and an Actor is an `actor` usage in the use case, once; between a Use Case and another part it is the `participants` link on the use case."
"An Association between anything else is not evidence of a connection and stays a review row. (Test_Vault_ Association approval, V1 participants; D-0038)"

"Tags on an EA Part whose disposition is `body` (PN, Piece Cost, Style, Quantity...) describe that use of the part in the assembly, so they are written as one `- On part <name>: tag: value; ...` line in the owning assembly's Source section, not lost with the usage and not copied to the part def. (V1 W-136, REG-142; D-0038)"

"A BindingConnector between two port usages of the same port def and the same conjugation is `bind a = b;`, and an ItemFlow InformationFlow between two port usages is `flow from a to b;`; both are placed like a connection (the common owner of the two Parts) and a port on a Part goes through the Part."
"Anything else is a review row with its own code."
"An EA Part tagged `isReference` is `ref part x : T;`."
"PDATA2 (redefinition) is recorded in the note and never applied."
"An Issue, Failure Mode or Use Case linked to an element writes the `affects` link on the note; no SysML is invented for it. (V1 relationships.yaml, W-288; D-0038, D-0039)"
"Every deferred element and connector leaves a flag in the vault, not only a CSV row."
"The flag goes on the note that owns the source (else the target) usage; a row with no note above it goes on one `modelCheck` holding note, \"Unplaced Review Items\", which has one flag per row."
"The Review CSVs stay."

"A usage or definition name keeps what makes the EA name different. A voltage puts its V at the decimal point and takes its sign as a letter: `+3.3VDC` is `P3V3DC`, `-13.3VDC` is `N13V3DC`, `12.5V` is `12V5`, `12VDC` stays `12VDC`; an unsigned voltage that starts the name takes `P`, because an identifier cannot start with a digit (`3.3VDC` is `P3V3DC`, so it and `+3.3VDC` meet and the second is told apart by its type)."

"Elsewhere a leading `+` is `plus`, a leading `-` is `minus`, a point between digits is `p`, `&` is `And`, `%` is `Pct`, `#` is `No`. A name that is only a number is named after its type (`wire1`, not `_1`)."
"Where the identifier is not just a respelling of the EA name, the EA name is recorded in `## Source: EA`."
"Two usages with one name take the name of their type to tell them apart (`a`, then `a_IConductor`); only a repeat of the same type takes `_2`."
"Quoted SysML names are not used, because every Workbench reader would need to change."
"Definitions keep the full EA title as their name."
"The importer can check a run before it writes: the full translation runs in memory and lists every flag, every deferred row and every problem, with a verdict."
"BLOCKED: the translation failed, a BOM error, or a file name the browser or Windows refuses."
"REVIEW: rows that would be skipped, conflicts with edits in the vault, BOM parts that differ from the vault, more than 10% of elements deferred, or over 50 BOM warnings."
"FLAGS: only flags."

"The check also says what becomes of every source row: standard; merged; imported but a value did not follow the standard (counted by code; nothing lost, something guessed); not in the model and may be lost (deferred or skipped by an error); text only; excluded by policy."
"It names the EA tables that are never read."

"An import into an existing vault shows the MDSE release, schema and every shipped plugin in the vault against the ones in the importer, with a state for each (same, newer in the importer, vault is newer, not installed, same version with different files)."
"Updating the toolset during the import is a choice: ticked by default only when the importer is newer, unticked when the vault is newer, forced on for a new vault."
"Unticked, the model is imported and the installed tools stay as they are."
"Ticked, it applies the same update as the maintenance section, with replaced files saved first."
"A part with no role name of its own in EA is named by its type and an index within its owner (`wire1`, `wire2`); a part that has an EA name keeps it."
"Replaces the type-title name of IMP-110 and the `_2` repeat of IMP-095 for parts."
"The vault holds the latest revision of each product in scope."
"Superseded revisions are not imported."
"One note per PartNumber. A part's properties come from its latest revision."
"A usage records the child revision pinned by the parent."
"Parent PN and line number identify a usage."
"A PN whose latest revision cannot be determined is reported and not imported."
"Revision strings are stored as exported, not normalized."
"A child part's body lists each assembly that uses an older revision of it, with that usage."
"A parent that pins a child revision different from the child's latest revision is flagged with `flagConflict`."
"Alternate-part rows with a blank PN attach to the PN above them."
"They are not parts."
"Drawing-only lines are recorded as document references and excluded from quantities."
"The importer reads the BOM from `.xlsx`, `.csv` or `.tsv` in the page."
"Two layouts are recognised by header names: flat (Parent Part Number, Child Part Number, Linenumber, Amount, Unit …) and redline (Number, CL1, CL2, level columns 0..7 or Structure)."
"Part numbers are read as text."

"In a redline, unstruck text in a cell is current and struck text is the previous value; a part number struck with no replacement is a removed line. A sheet with no recognised header is refused with the reason."
"The redline layout was checked against the four real redlines"

"Each part number gets one `Object` (subtype part) note named `<PN>` (the part number alone, so the file name and the part number are the same value; the name is the H1 and a `- Name:` line in Source) under `BOM/Parts`: `part def P_<PN>` with `partNumber`, `revision` (CL1+CL2 as exported), `source`, `lifecycleState` attributes."

"The parent's block owns one part usage per line: whole-number counts with unit ea/piece become multiplicity; any other quantity is `quantity` plus the unit as written (case kept); line, pinned `childRevision`, reference designator, effectivity dates, SSC and notes are attributes."
"Drawing lines (name starts DWG) become a `Document` note under `BOM/Drawings` referenced from the parent and are not usages."
"Alternate-source rows attach to the line above."
"Parent note lists children in `hasPart`."
"The latest revision of a part number is the one it has as an assembly, or the one every parent pins when it is only a child."

"When there are several, or two revisions each have lines, the part number and the lines that use it are not imported and an error finding names the revisions (BOM-009, BOM-002). A parent pinning an older child revision gets a `flagConflict`; the child's body lists its older-revision users."
"Part numbers already noted in the vault are left as they are."
"Findings go to `99_System/11_Import/BOM Findings <date>.md`."

"EA to BOM matching by part number appearing in one EA element name, EA alias or PN tag is a report only. A part number that is already in the vault is kept; if the new file disagrees with it on any line (pinned revision, count or quantity, or a line that is new) the finding `EXISTING_DIFFERS` names the first lines that differ and nothing is rewritten."
"Each importer and its clean base vault are a matched pair with one release version, checked before planning or writing (mdse_release in .vault.yaml)."
"During pre-release the Base Vault pins the latest released Workbench; a newer candidate is recorded as `candidateVersion` in the release manifest."
"Plugin stack reviewed as a dependency surface"
"Dataview removed from the controlled runtime after replacement and startup-cost gates passed (no Dataview queries in the vault"
"Bases + Workbench cover it)."
"Conflicts with older docs that still name Dataview (C-14)."
"A pre-release integration Base Vault may pin the declared Workbench candidate; an issued release may not."

"The Base Vault ships Bootstrap, the Workbench, Templater 2.25.0, Advanced Canvas 7.1.0 and Obsidian Git 2.40.0, each unmodified from its release, listed in `community-plugins.json`, pinned with version, source, licence, governed settings and SHA-256 of main.js, manifest.json and styles.css in `plugin-lock.yaml` (status line removed; nothing is `not_bundled`)."
"`data.json` is seeded from the governed settings and never overwritten by an update."
"Core plugins are the V1 set with Templates off."
"`99_System/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names each licence."

"Controlled runtime dependencies need explicit value: essential = Bootstrap, Workbench, Templater, Advanced Canvas, Obsidian Git; provisional = Fileclass, Breadcrumbs; review for retirement = Dataview."
"Bootstrap runs after the person trusts the vault, about two seconds after layout."

"It checks each locked plugin's files against the lock, enables those that match, merges the lock's governed settings into their `data.json` (the person's other keys stay), enables required and switches off prohibited core plugins, and reports what it did in one notice. A plugin whose hash differs or whose file is missing stays off and is named."
"It never downloads."
"The command \"Check and repair this vault\" runs it again."
"When `.vault.yaml` has no author, Bootstrap asks for a full name once, derives the author code, writes `author:` and creates the person note."
"Obsidian's \"Trust author and enable plugins\" choice is stored outside the vault and cannot be set by any file, so Bootstrap can only act after it is made."
"The Edit lens adds relationships, elements and requirement text."
"Relationship kinds offered depend on the selected note's SysML definition; targets come from a searchable, folder-grouped browser limited to eligible notes."
"Structure and links are written into the source note's `## SysML v2` block"

"Every Edit-lens change is previewed as a diff, applied only on a click, refused when the file differs from what the preview was built from, written atomically (all files or none), and undoable while the files are unchanged."

"A new note's id is the class prefix plus the highest existing number plus one (MOD-007); its uid is local time plus the author code from `.vault.yaml` and moves forward one millisecond on a clash (MOD-004)."
"Without an author code, adding an element is refused."

"A relationship can be selected from the Workbench list, a relationship table row or a canvas line (the canvas edge id carries the relationship's location) and then changed, given properties, or removed."
"The kinds that can be changed are those the Edit lens can add; any other member can only be removed or edited in the note."

"Relationship properties are written inside the relationship in SysML: a `doc` comment, `attribute name = value;` (or `attribute name { doc … }` when the value is not a plain number or simple text), usage modifiers `ordered` and `nonunique`, quantity and direction."
"The drop-down offers only the options that relationship has; a free attribute name is accepted only where the relationship allows it (not specializes or verifies)."
"Renaming a usage is refused when its name is used elsewhere in the block."

"Every option in the Edit lens has a \"?\" that shows a short bundled definition with its options and a link to the language note (`99_System/04_Language`); nothing is fetched. A form being filled is not discarded when the index refreshes."
"The Edit lens has a Ports tab for a part, item, port or interface definition."

"It adds, changes and removes: port definition features (`in|out|inout item|attribute|port`), port usages (`[ref] port p : [~]PortDef [mult] [ordered] [nonunique]`), interface definition ends (`end e : [~]PortDef`), connections (`connect`, `connection [n] [: Def] connect`, `interface [n] [: Def] connect`, with optional `end ::>` bindings), flows (`flow [n] [of Item] from a.x to b.y`) and bindings (`bind a.x = b.y`)."
"Types are chosen in the searchable browser; paths are offered from the owner's parts and their ports."
"Every option has a \"?\"."

"The Ports tab checks before it previews: names are unique in the owner, a port or end is typed by a port definition, only items and attributes have a direction, a path must resolve through the owner's usages (inherited ones included), an interface connection joins ports, each port matches its end's type and conjugation, and a flow starts at an out (or inout) feature and ends at an in (or inout) one, with every `~` on the path reversing directions."

"Type or end mismatches that SysML allows (bound features of different types, both ports unconjugated) are shown as notes, not refusals. A member that has a body (properties, description) is not rewritten by the Ports tab."

"The scanner reads every port form: `~`, `ref`, `:>` and `:>>` before or after the multiplicity, `ordered`, `nonunique`, directed features, interface and connection ends, and plain, `connection` and `interface` connects."
"Changing an owned usage in the Relationships tab keeps its `~`, `ref`, `:>` and `:>>`."
"After an apply or an undo the Edit lens redraws its lists from the new index without discarding a form being filled."
"The Edit lens Merge tab marks aliases and merges them in two steps."

"An alias is marked from the open note or from matches found between BOM parts and EA notes: the EA part number (`- PN:` or `- Part Number:`) equal to the BOM number, then the number inside the EA title, then a close name; only the first two with a single candidate are ticked for the person."
"Merge needs an alias, so nothing merges without being marked and reviewed."
"A merge keeps the surviving note's file name, id, uid and SysML package."

"The removed note's content is folded in: frontmatter (more specific subtype, EA class, tags and relationship fields combined), user text under `## Merged from <title>`, Source lines combined without repeats, SysML members carried over with the removed definition's symbol rewritten to the survivor's and its specializations added. A member both notes define differently stays in the survivor and the other is kept under `## Not carried over from <title>` as sysml text."
"The removed title is listed under `## Aliases` and its id and uid under `## Former ids`."

"A merge rewrites every other note: `[[Removed]]` becomes `[[Kept|Removed]]` in text (frontmatter lists get the plain new name, without repeats or links to itself) and the removed definition's symbol becomes the kept one in every SysML block. A chain of aliases resolves to its end; many aliases merge in one preview, with the changed files counted, the removed files listed and one Undo that brings them all back. A note with more than one definition, a survivor with no SysML block and notes of different classes are refused with the reason."
"A YAML link that repeats a relationship the SysML block already states (the BOM importer lists `hasPart` in both) is one relationship."
"Counting both doubled every quantity in the rolled-up parts list."

"The rolled-up parts list multiplies counts down the assembly and keeps measured amounts (`quantity` with `unit`) apart by unit; a count and a length are never added. A quantity of 0 is a document line and adds nothing."
"Structure shows a measured amount where a count would be. (BOM-016, D-0040)"
"The Workbench keeps structure, design types, internal structure, function, states and requirements apart."
"Structure shows parts only."
"Design types shows only what a definition specializes and what specializes it."

"Internal shows the parts with the ports each part's type offers (inherited ones included), the definition's own ports, and every connection, binding and flow with both ends resolved; an end that names a part or port that does not exist is marked."
"Function shows actions and States shows states, each drawn alone."
"Requirements shows the trace around the selected note."
"The Obsidian panel has the same lenses."
"Every section of a note view and every list group folds."
"Each page has Collapse all and Expand all; which sections are open is kept while the person moves between notes."
"The Notes list can be grouped by type or folder, each group folded."
"Measured quantities print their unit (`[1.5 Meter]`)."
"Every AI process has a written instruction file and an ID."
"The index is in `AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md`."
"AI processes do not edit model files unless the process is a note-creation process under R-2.x."
"Changelog review (AI-CR-01) is report-only."
"AI does not create or split vaults."
"It may recommend a split."
"AI does not invent source facts."
"Code enters this repository only with tests that run in CI."
"Carried code keeps its original tests."
"Workbench candidate CI runs a 10,000-note semantic-cache scale smoke (completion/memory regression gate, not timing)."
"Canvas geometry is presentation only."
"It never creates a semantic relationship."
